FRENCH — MOCK EXAM #15
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: FRENCH
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Active Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Active Listening.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Active Listening.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active Listening.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Active Listening.

2. “Bonjour” is used to say: (1 mark)
   A. Thank you
   B. Good morning / hello
   C. Excuse me
   D. Good night only

3. When practising Oral expression, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Oral expression.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Oral expression.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral expression.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Oral expression.

4. When practising Listening for information Vocabulary Grammar Attention, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for information Vocabulary Grammar Attention.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening for information Vocabulary Grammar Attention.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for information Vocabulary Grammar Attention.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening for information Vocabulary Grammar Attention.

5. The French word for “book” is: (1 mark)
   A. livre
   B. fenêtre
   C. chaise
   D. porte

6. When practising Listening for information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening for information.

   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for information.

   C. Copy random text without understanding Interactive Speaking.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Interactive Speaking.

8. When practising Interactive speaking 1.2 Oral expression 1.3 Interactive listening 1.3 Active li, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive speaking 1.2 Oral expression 1.3 Interactive listening 1.3 Active li.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive speaking 1.2 Oral expression 1.3 Interactive listening 1.3 Active li.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Interactive speaking 1.2 Oral expression 1.3 Interactive listening 1.3 Active li.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Interactive speaking 1.2 Oral expression 1.3 Interactive listening 1.3 Active li.

9. When practising Interactive listening 1.3 Active listening 1.4 Listening for information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Interactive listening 1.3 Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive listening 1.3 Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Interactive listening 1.3 Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive listening 1.3 Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.

   A. Use insults to “practise” Interactive speaking.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive speaking.
